correctness.rationale: For the repaired tail claim, independently checked all three integrated Lagrange denominators and numerator F; L is the exact dual sup-norm amplification. On p,r<delta the positive numerators make only the middle weight negative and yield 1+2F/(pr). The product sublevel area is epsilon(1+log(delta^2/epsilon)); using g±delta with x-domains [0,1-2delta] and [0,1] gives matching scaled bounds after delta tends to zero. A fixed positive lower bound on one spacing leaves an O_delta(1/t) tail. The coefficient is 12 integral g=2 and layer cake gives the moment cutoff including divergence at q=1. The frozen sign integrations were also verified directly; their omission is for overlap, not error. Frozen verification and script inspected, not executed. The bounded area argument, not finite checks, establishes the limit.

value.rationale: The norm measures worst-case amplification of bounded sample errors in a natural minimal random-node rule. The sharp coefficient and logarithmic enhancement distinguish simultaneous close spacings from a single collision and establish a concrete moment cutoff (including infinite mean) rather than an arbitrary numerical stability statistic. No universal fixed-integrand error claim is made.
